title: Morning Brief
intro_md: Type **more on G3** (or any code) in April's chat, or tap **More info** here and paste the request there, and she'll dig in.

items.headline_md: **Israel** election: **Netanyahu**'s bloc falls short of a majority
items.summary_md: Final results give Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats, the opposition 48 and Arab-led parties a historic 19, so nobody has the 61 needed and coalition talks look long.

items.headline_md: **Saudi** air defenses intercept **Houthi** missiles aimed at Riyadh
items.summary_md: The Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed two ballistic missiles fired toward Riyadh, while the Houthis say Saudi airstrikes killed 27 people in Yemen.

items.headline_md: Rare truce lets aid into Russian-occupied **Oleshky**, **Ukraine**
items.summary_md: A humanitarian operation is under way in the occupied town, though there are serious doubts evacuees will be allowed to reach Ukrainian-held territory.

items.headline_md: **Bank of Japan** says inflation finally hit its 2% target
items.summary_md: It's the first time in more than 13 years since adopting the goal, but the bank held off on raising rates for now.

items.headline_md: **Binance** hit by a record $6.3B hack
items.summary_md: The exchange says a compromised engineer's laptop may have let an attacker submit withdrawals; about $3B is frozen, it pledged to cover losses, and a US firm points to North Korea.

items.headline_md: **Amazon** misses on earnings as AI spending drains cash
items.summary_md: Q3 EPS was $1.89 vs. $1.96 expected and revenue $201.94B vs. $202.31B; trailing free cash flow swung to −$42.4B, though AWS grew 39% and Jassy promises to spend meaningfully more in 2027.

items.headline_md: **Intel** plunges after warning it will burn cash
items.summary_md: Shares fell more than 25% premarket after Intel cited a weak PC market, manufacturing bottlenecks and heavy spending, per Reuters.

items.headline_md: Update: **DoorDash** agrees to buy **Instacart** for about $17B
items.summary_md: The talks became a deal at $65 per share, at least 75% cash, with Instacart's brand and app kept; closing is expected by late 2027 or the first half of 2028.

items.headline_md: **BP** profit quadruples on Iran-war refining margins
items.summary_md: BP beat forecasts and cut net debt by $8.4B ahead of a December strategy update; Shell also nearly doubled its quarterly profit.

items.headline_md: **Planet of Lana II** goes free-to-start on mobile
items.summary_md: The sequel is in Android Early Access with a free opening and a one-time $8.99 unlock, a switch from the first game's fully paid launch; iOS pre-orders are coming.

items.headline_md: **Monster Hunter Outlanders** is out on iOS and Android
items.summary_md: Tencent's full third-person Monster Hunter for phones launched with co-op for up to four players and a new region, Aesoland.

items.headline_md: **Darkest Dungeon II** is coming to mobile in 2027
items.summary_md: Playdigious is porting the dark-fantasy roguelike to iOS and Android.

items.headline_md: Mobile's Halloween events: **Clash of Clans**, **Monopoly Go**, **Fortnite** and more
items.summary_md: PocketGamer.biz rounds up how Supercell, Scopely, Epic, King, The Pokémon Company and others are dressing up live games for the season, a handy reference for seasonal live-ops ideas.

sections.title: Video Game Emulation
sections.body_md: No PS5 or Switch 2 breakthrough today. Wii U general lifter watch: still no public repo or release from the r/decomps poster (checked GitHub and the web; the only new hit, CafeRecomp, is a separate BOTW-only Wii U recomp that isn't playable yet). Reddit's r/decomps feed was blocked again, so it wasn't read directly.

items.headline_md: Update: **TotK Recomp**, a second **Tears of the Kingdom** PC recomp, is out in beta
items.summary_md: valentderah's native Windows port builds from your own 1.2.1 or 1.4.3 dump and runs at 60 fps or more up to 4K with mouse, gamepad and gyro; crashes and visual bugs are expected.

items.headline_md: **Super Smash Bros. Ultimate** runs natively on PC via **WindowSmash**
items.summary_md: The Switch recomp builds a Windows program from your own 13.0.5 dump and keys, with up to eight controllers, DLC fighters and relayed online play; matches are still lightly tested.

items.headline_md: **CPS-2 Recomp** 1.0 brings 17 Capcom arcade games to PC with rollback
items.summary_md: Street Fighter Alpha, Vampire Savior, Marvel vs. Capcom and more leave beta with two-player online rollback across Windows, Mac, Linux and Steam Deck; you need your own ROM sets.

items.headline_md: **DS Kart Recompiled** turns **Mario Kart DS** into a native Windows game
items.summary_md: Version 0.1.0 translates both DS processors to C and builds from your own EU cartridge, with 4x 3D, up to 240 fps and LAN play.

items.headline_md: Update: **Brawl Recompiled** 0.5.0 pushes **Smash Bros. Brawl** to 240 fps
items.summary_md: The native Wii-to-PC port adds the frame-rate bump after last week's online play, with Project+ mods loading as on a Wii.

items.headline_md: **Zone of the Enders** recompiled from PS2 to Windows
items.summary_md: ZOE-Recompiled 1.0 uses PS2Recomp for 60 fps, widescreen, save states and two-player Versus from your own US disc.

items.headline_md: Halloween weekend (Oct 30–Nov 1): **You Can See Everything** vs. **Clayface** for No. 1
items.summary_md: With Halloween on Saturday and no major openers, Gold Derby predicts You Can See Everything $14M, Clayface $12M, Wildwood $7M, Wicker $4M and Street Fighter $4M.

items.headline_md: **You Can See Everything** keeps beating forecasts
items.summary_md: A24's Elizabeth Holmes documentary rose 25% in its second weekend and sits at $45.1M domestic, topping its forecast every week so far.

items.headline_md: Last weekend: **Clayface** won with $24M
items.summary_md: Warner Bros. and DC's body-horror origin story earned an A-minus CinemaScore, but horror tends to suffer on Halloween itself.

items.headline_md: New this week: **Everest: The Other Side** and **The Only Living Pickpocket in New York** review well
items.summary_md: Disney's Imax doc is Certified Fresh at 88% (Metacritic 65), and John Turturro's crime drama, expanding this week, has 96% (Metacritic 80).

items.headline_md: **Patrick Stewart** dies at 86
items.summary_md: The Star Trek and X-Men star died at home in Los Angeles; Ian McKellen, William Shatner and Hugh Jackman are among those paying tribute.

items.headline_md: **Nvidia** releases open-weight **Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe**
items.summary_md: The speech model transcribes 40 languages, translates 31 to or from English and handles recordings up to an hour with up to eight speakers.

items.headline_md: **OpenAI** and **ServiceNow** widen their deal
items.summary_md: OpenAI models and agents will act inside ServiceNow software, starting with a ServiceNow plugin for ChatGPT that's available now.

items.headline_md: **Mistral** releases weights for its trillion-parameter model
items.summary_md: TechCrunch reports the open-weight release is aimed at cybersecurity.

items.headline_md: **Amazon** will sell its **Trainium** AI chips externally in late 2027
items.summary_md: Jassy said the chips business is growing triple digits year over year and AWS will be a $1T revenue business within five to 10 years.

items.headline_md: **Reddit** is moving to a mostly logged-in experience
items.summary_md: Search referrals fell by more than 1M a week in October; Reddit will test the change outside the US this quarter, while Q3 revenue rose 53% to $895M and ad revenue 54%.

items.headline_md: **GM** settles for $220M over selling drivers' private data
items.summary_md: TechCrunch reports the settlement over GM's sale of driver data.

items.headline_md: **Meta** quietly launches **Style Sketch**, an AI fashion app
items.summary_md: It's a new standalone AI app from Meta, per TechCrunch.

items.headline_md: Fan-fiction site **AO3** could be offline for up to 4 weeks
items.summary_md: Archive of Our Own went down after a security incident, TechCrunch reports.
Quoted at 4:14 AM AZ (7:14 ET) by Reuters, as Amazon and Intel deepen worries about AI spending; the Nasdaq-100 is on track to erase about $950B.

items.headline_md: **Intel** down more than 25%, **Amazon** −6.3% premarket
items.summary_md: Same Reuters report, 4:14 AM AZ; Alphabet slipped another 0.6% after its record selloff.

items.headline_md: **Bitcoin** −4% to $77,465 after the Binance hack
items.summary_md: Ether also fell 4% to $2,239.80 and BNB 5% to $702.28, per CNBC's Friday morning update.

items.headline_md: **Brent** crosses $116, **WTI** tops $103
items.summary_md: Moneycontrol ties the jump to supply fears after attacks on Saudi Arabia.
Quoted at 5:07 AM AZ; it's back below $4,000.

items.headline_md: **Phoenix**: storms, high near 75, low around 64; ⚠️ Flood Watch
items.summary_md: Showers and thunderstorms, heaviest noon to 5 PM, 100% chance with ¾ to 1 inch of rain possible; Flood Watches run until 6 PM today and until 5 AM Monday Nov 2.

items.headline_md: **Show Low**: storms later, high near 62, low around 43; ⚠️ Flood Watch
items.summary_md: Slight chance of storms 11 AM–2 PM, then showers and thunderstorms (90%) continuing tonight; gusts to 22 mph; Flood Watch until 5 AM Monday Nov 2.

items.headline_md: **Snowflake**: storms later, high near 66, low around 43; ⚠️ Flood Watch
items.summary_md: Slight chance of storms 11 AM–2 PM, then showers and thunderstorms (80%) through about 5 AM; gusts to 24 mph; Flood Watch until 5 AM Monday Nov 2.

items.headline_md: **OpenAI**'s updated Model Spec
items.summary_md: A rare plain-language look at how one major lab now wants its models to weigh your intent, harm, honesty and agency when instructions run out.
